problems.basis: BE/AI reviewed (#16 R1). Every code in the Problem.code enum, one fixture per code holding that code's DEFAULT face. apps/api ProblemFixtureContractTest now pins type/title/status/retryable to io.nullnull.shared.problem.ProblemCode, so these four can no longer drift from what the server answers with; the review found APPLY_FAILED carrying retryable true, which contradicted both the enum and docs/api/README.md's statement that only ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and RATE_LIMITED are retryable. requestId is a UUIDv7 because that is what RequestIdFilter generates (the earlier ULID was a shape the server never produces on its own). NOT verified here: `detail` is the contract's English fallback and is deliberately generic rather than the literal sentence a given throw site uses (README says the raising slice owns that sentence, and FE renders its own copy from `code`); `instance` is a plausible path, not a captured one, except for DELETION_STATUS_EXPIRED which has exactly one throw site. NOT COVERED: the codes README's UI mapping table gives a second status - INVALID_REQUEST 400/405/406/413/415, LOCK_CONFLICT 409/422, APPLY_FAILED 500/503 - have no variant fixture, because the index is keyed by code and holds one entry per code. 11 of the 23 codes have no throw site in apps/api yet.

session.basis: Bootstrap trio needed to exercise the 401 retry and CSRF reissue policies. deletion-receipt.statusUrl now carries the /api/v1 server base, matching what DeletionService actually emits; it previously omitted it and the contract constrained neither, so both spellings passed. The contract now describes statusUrl as an API path and DeletionIT pins its prefix to spring.mvc.servlet.path so the literal and the configured path cannot drift. BE/AI reviewed (#16 R1): DeletionStatus is a plain record with no @JsonInclude, so the server really does send completedAt, failureCode and retryable rather than omitting them, and the fixture's retryable false with status RUNNING matches the rule that retryable is true exactly while status is PARTIAL_FAILED. Three more DeletionRequestStatus fixtures cover COMPLETED, PARTIAL_FAILED and FAILED: every field is decided by apps/api (JdbcDeletionStore.markCompleted clears failureCode and sets completedAt; markFailed sets completedAt only when the status is FAILED), so FAILED carries a completedAt while PARTIAL_FAILED does not - which is exactly why terminality is read from status and never from completedAt. These are derived from the server's own write paths rather than invented, but no captured response backs them, so serverVerified stays false.

trips.basis: BE/AI authored. candidates is empty while candidateCount is 5 on purpose: the contract states that candidates is a bounded view and listTripCandidates is the paginated source, so the array length is never the total. trip-detail-interests is its own trip with its own trip-page entry, not a second face of trip-detail-scheduled. They previously shared one id AND version 3 while holding different day items, which made the ETag - a quoted trip version - claim one validator for two materially different bodies. Each detail fixture now maps to exactly one row in trip-page.json, and the openapi.yaml response examples are generated from these files and pinned to them by packages/contracts/scripts/check-examples.mjs. The places inside day items now use the HS/11 pair like the places set: categoryCode and regionCode are opaque and provider-derived per the contract, so an invented taxonomy such as ATTRACTION/KR-11-110 does not satisfy it. Only 경복궁's HS/11 came from an actual detailCommon2 call; the others share its SHAPE and are not themselves verified provider values.

optimizations.basis: NO approved example exists for listOptimizationHistory. Values invented to match Figma S14 422:2925 (applied/kept/reverted, and an empty variant) and validated against the schema only. Replace with BE/AI's real response (BA-053).

places.basis: BE/AI authored from the approved searchPlaces contract. Shapes match the server projection, including sourceAttribution read from the reviewed source registry revision and the categoryName/regionName that stay null until a reviewed code-to-label mapping exists. categoryCode/regionCode are opaque machine values and must not be rendered; only 경복궁's HS/11 came from an actual detailCommon2 call (#109), the others share its shape. Still not a captured server response, so serverVerified stays false until BA-022 has one. Place codes use the HS/11 pair: categoryCode and regionCode are opaque and provider-derived per the contract, so an invented taxonomy does not satisfy it. Only 경복궁's HS/11 came from an actual detailCommon2 call - the others share its SHAPE and are not themselves verified provider values. categoryName and regionName are null because JdbcCatalogPlaceQuery returns null for both until a reviewed code-to-label mapping exists; a fixture that fills them promises a label the server cannot produce.

placeDetail.basis: BE/AI authored from the server projection (PlaceController.PlaceDetailResponse.from) so FE can build getPlace before the route opens. description/thumbnailUrl/thumbnailAsset are null because the collector requests overviewYN=N and firstImageYN=N, so overview text and images are never stored — an example with rich text there would break on first real integration. categoryCode/regionCode reuse 경복궁's HS/11, the only pair that came from an actual detailCommon2 call (#109). externalId is the placeholder KTO-PENDING-CAPTURE and location uses public reference coordinates: neither came from a captured response, so do not treat them as provider evidence. Note getPlace is fail-closed behind NULLNULL_CATALOG_PUBLIC_ENABLED=false until BA-021-T3 staging evidence exists, so this fixture is the only shape FE can build against today.
